q: How does the ground-space fidelity we obtained under the S_N permutation-basis encoding (0.997 at N=5) compare quantitatively with the paper's L=N*ceil(log2 N) qubit bit-string encoding under a scan of the C1, C2 penalty coefficients? A mismatch of a few percent might hide an unfavorable penalty-scaling regime that the paper does not report.
basis: We deliberately implemented the S_N permutation basis rather than the bit-string basis with penalty projectors C1, C2 the paper uses. The paper does not report a sensitivity scan over the penalty coefficients, and our headline fidelity (0.997) may not transfer literally to the bit-string encoding.
next_steps: Re-implement H_P in the L-qubit bit-string encoding with explicit C1, C2 penalty terms; sweep lambda_1, lambda_2 in [0.1, 100]; compare final fidelity, energy gap, and time-to-solution vs the S_N-basis result at N=4, 5.

q: Does the interior minimum gap change qualitatively if the driver Hamiltonian H_D is switched from the adjacent-transposition Cayley mixer of S_N to the full-transposition (Star / Bubble) Cayley mixer, or to a data-dependent mixer that respects Aut(G)?
basis: Our driver used the adjacent-transposition Cayley graph. This is the natural choice but is not the only S_N mixer; the paper's transverse-field driver on qubits is topologically different (hypercube). We saw evidence that endpoint degeneracy from Aut(G) can dominate.
next_steps: Implement all three drivers on the same H_P; sweep N=4..6, plot min interior gap and adiabatic runtime; check whether an Aut(G)-adapted mixer removes the schedule-endpoint degeneracy and improves the empirical adiabatic runtime.

q: How does the automorphism-induced ground-space degeneracy of H_P at s=1 (|Iso| = |Aut(G)| for isomorphic pairs) scale with N, and does it interfere with adiabatic preparation as N grows, or does the algorithm just deposit uniform mass over Iso as in our C_4 (N=4) case where all 8 automorphism orbit representatives were populated uniformly?
basis: In our C_4 test all 8 automorphism eigenstates were populated to a near-uniform 1/8 each, and the s=1 gap was 0 as a result of degeneracy. The paper mentions automorphism enumeration as a feature but does not explicitly analyze whether this Aut-induced degeneracy hurts adiabatic preparation at large N.
next_steps: Systematic sweep over graph families with controlled |Aut(G)| (Cayley graphs, cycle graphs, Kneser graphs) at N=4..7; measure fidelity on Iso as a function of |Aut(G)| and N; check whether uniform-orbit population survives at larger N.

q: Is the residual expected H_P energy at s=1 for non-isomorphic pairs (in our path-vs-star control, exactly 4.0 = minimum possible edge mismatch) a reliable numerical proxy for graph edit distance / maximum common subgraph? If so, adiabatic-GI generalizes automatically to approximate-GI, an application the paper does not develop.
basis: Our N=5 path-vs-K1,4 control converged exactly to H_P_min = 4, matching the true classical minimum symmetric edge-mismatch count over all 120 permutations. This is a byproduct of the adiabatic evolution finding the ground state of H_P regardless of whether it is zero.
next_steps: Construct graph pairs of increasing edit distance (Erdos-Renyi + k random rewires); run the same AQA; correlate final E_{H_P} with the classically-computed graph edit distance; check monotonicity and slope.

q: For known-hard GI instances (cospectral, non-isomorphic strongly-regular families such as Praust or Miyazaki graphs) at N=6, 7, does the interior minimum gap close super-polynomially in N?, since the paper explicitly declines to report Delta(N) scaling but such families are the canonical stress test for algorithmic GI approaches.
basis: The paper says Delta(N) at large N is a fundamental open problem in AQC and does not test SRG-family instances. Our N=5 non-iso control (path vs star) has a large 0.014 interior gap because the degree sequences differ; SRG-cospectral pairs remove that easy distinguisher.
next_steps: Enumerate small cospectral non-isomorphic pairs at N=6 (720 dim) and N=7 (5040 dim) using saucy/nauty; run the same S_N adiabatic simulator; fit gap vs N; compare to the polynomial-runtime hope of the paper.
